Gettysburg.wildlife_intro:
Gettysburg's calls are shaped by the battlefield at its doorstep: groundhogs burrowing fence lines and park-edge yards, raccoons in the borough's historic chimneys, skunks under porches throughout, and bats in the attics of the battle-era housing. Parkland wildlife presses into every borough street.

The Gettysburg year runs in waves. Cold months drive squirrels and rodents into attics, and big brown bats overwinter quietly in wall voids across the older housing. Spring opens raccoon denning season and groundhog digging, summer brings bat maternity colonies — Pennsylvania Game Commission guidance treats May 15 through August 1 as the window when exclusions should wait — and fall sends a second wave of squirrels and rodents looking for winter rooms. Our crew starts with a full inspection, then removes the animals and seals every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds. Historic homes need masonry-respecting sealing planned at inspection, and park-edge lots need ground-level denning checked with the roofline.
